query: adaptive user simulator reward design LLM agents
text:
1. **[UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning](https://lifelongagent.github.io/Project-Lifelong-Agent/UserRL/index.html)** — A close match: studies how simulated users, turn-level reward assignment, and trajectory scoring affect LLM-agent training. **People:** Cheng Qian and Heng Ji (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Jielin Qiu, Zhiwei Liu, Haolin Chen, Shirley Kokane, Weiran Yao, Shelby Heinecke, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, and Huan Wang (Salesforce AI Research).

2. **[UserLM-R1: Modeling Human Reasoning in User Language Models with Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.09215v1)** — Combines dynamic user goals, strategic reasoning, and multiple rewards to build adaptable simulators resistant to agent manipulation. **People:** Feng Zhang, Shijia Li, Chunmao Zhang, Zhanyu Ma, Jun Xu, Jiuchong Gao, Jinghua Hao, Renqing He, Jingwen Xu, and Han Liu. **Affiliations represented:** Meituan, Peking University, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, and Dalian University of Technology.

3. **[Learning User Simulators with Turing Rewards](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.19336v1)** — Directly addresses simulator reward design: an LLM judge rewards responses that are indistinguishable from a particular human user’s responses, conditioned on their history. **People:** Yingshan Susan Wang, Cedegao E. Zhang, Linlu Qiu, Zexue He, Pengyuan Li, Alex Pentland, Roger P. Levy, and Yoon Kim. **Affiliations represented:** MIT, Stanford University, and MIT–IBM Watson AI Lab.

4. **[MIMESIS: Learning User Simulators as Training Environments for Interactive Agents](https://viethoang1512.github.io/mimesis/)** — Trains realistic user behaviors, then uses simulator interactions and private reasoning to provide rewards and coaching for agent training. **People:** Hoang Phan (Meta and NYU), Changdae Oh (Meta and University of Wisconsin–Madison), and Dat Huynh, Andrey Zhmoginov, Qi Zeng, Wancen Mu, Yue Cao, Shengjie Bi, Yun He, and Deren Lei. **Lead affiliation:** Meta Superintelligence Labs.

query: within-run and across-run adaptation agent training
text:
1. **[Learning to Learn-at-Test-Time: Language Agents with Learnable Adaptation Policies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.00830)** (2026). A close match: Meta-TTL combines adaptation across successive episodes with an outer training loop that learns better adaptation policies. **People:** Zhanzhi Lou, Hui Chen, Yibo Li, Qian Wang, and Bryan Hooi — National University of Singapore.

2. **[Meta-RL Induces Exploration in Language Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.16848)** (2025). Trains agents across episodes to explore, reflect on feedback, and improve subsequent attempts through in-context adaptation. **People:** Yulun Jiang — EPFL and ETH Zurich; Liangze Jiang — EPFL and Idiap Research Institute; Damien Teney — Idiap; Michael Moor — ETH Zurich; Maria Brbić — EPFL.

3. **[Beyond Final Scores: A Systematic Evaluation of Agents for Long-Horizon AI Research and Development](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13417)** (2026). Directly examines within-run behavior and experience reuse within and across tasks; especially relevant for evaluating whether adaptation actually helps. **People:** Yiwei Li and colleagues — Meituan; Wanli Yang, Hexiang Tan, and Fei Sun — University of Chinese Academy of Sciences.

4. **[Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366)** (2023). Foundational work on improving across trials using stored verbal reflections without updating model weights. **People:** Noah Shinn, Federico Cassano, and Edward Berman — Northeastern University; Ashwin Gopinath — MIT; Karthik Narasimhan and Shunyu Yao — Princeton University.

1. **[SEAL: Synergistic Co-Evolution of Agents and Learning Environments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24426)** — May 2026. Jointly improves tool-use agents and their learning interfaces using diagnoses of failed interactions. **People:** Yihao Hu, Zhihao Wen, Xiujin Liu, Pan Wang, Xin Zhang, and Wei Wu. **Affiliations:** Ant Group, Westlake University, University of Michigan–Ann Arbor, and University of Science and Technology of China.

2. **[GenEnv: Difficulty-Aligned Co-Evolution Between LLM Agents and Environment Simulators](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19682)** — December 2025. A generative simulator learns to create tasks matched to an agent’s changing capabilities. **People and affiliations:** Jiacheng Guo, Jiahao Qiu, and Mengdi Wang (Princeton); Ling Yang (Princeton and ByteDance Seed); Peter Chen (Columbia); Qixin Xiao and Xinzhe Juan (University of Michigan); Yinjie Wang (University of Chicago); Ke Shen (ByteDance Seed).

3. **[Agent-World: Scaling Real-World Environment Synthesis for Evolving General Agent Intelligence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18292)** — April 2026. Combines environment and task discovery with reinforcement learning, generating new tasks around agents’ capability gaps. **People:** Guanting Dong, Junting Lu, Junjie Huang, Wanjun Zhong, and colleagues, including Ji-Rong Wen and Zhicheng Dou. **Affiliations:** Renmin University of China and ByteDance Seed.

4. **[Co-Evolution in Agentic Systems: Toward Self-Directed Evolution Beyond Human Design](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10299)** — August 2026. A recent survey covering agent–environment co-evolution across tasks, feedback, and interaction spaces. **People:** Qing Zong, Jiayu Liu, Junhao Shen, Zecong Tang, Linsi Wu, Yuxuan Liu, Rui Wang, Zhaowei Wang, Weiqi Wang, Cheng Qian, Xiusi Chen, and Yangqiu Song. **Affiliations:** HKUST, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Chinese University of Hong Kong, University of Hong Kong, and Peking University.

Closely related work that progressively increases environment difficulty and schedules environments during agent training. **People:** Zhiyuan Fan, Tinghao Yu, Yuanjun Cai, Jiang Zhou, Jiangtao Guan, Jincheng Liu, Yun Yang, Dingxin Hu, Zhuo Han, Xing Wu, Feng Zhang, and Lilin Wang. **Affiliation listed:** Tencent Hunyuan Team.

query: multi-turn reinforcement learning user simulation benchmarks
text:
1. **[LMRL Gym: Benchmarks for Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning with Language Models](https://lmrl-gym.github.io/static/paper.pdf)** — Eight interactive tasks covering dialogue and text games, with simulators for RL training and evaluation. **People:** Marwa Abdulhai, Isadora White, Charlie Snell, Charles Sun, Joey Hong, Yuexiang Zhai, and Sergey Levine (**UC Berkeley**); Kelvin Xu (**Google DeepMind**).

2. **[UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.19736v1)** — Eight standardized environments combining simulated users, multi-turn RL, and benchmarking of clarification, persuasion, planning, and tool use. **People:** Cheng Qian (**Salesforce AI Research; UIUC**), Heng Ji (**UIUC**), and collaborators including Zuxin Liu, Weiran Yao, Shelby Heinecke, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, and Huan Wang (**Salesforce AI Research**).

3. **[SalesSim: Benchmarking and Aligning Multimodal Language Models as Retail User Simulators](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.08334v1)** — Benchmarks persona-driven shoppers in multi-turn retail conversations; introduces UserGRPO to improve simulator fidelity through RL. **People:** Yada Pruksachatkun and Chien-Sheng Wu (**Salesforce Research**); Elaine Wan, Lyanna Chen, and Kai-Wei Chang (**UCLA**).

4. **[MUA-RL: Multi-turn User-interacting Agent Reinforcement Learning for Agentic Tool Use](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18669v1)** — Integrates simulated users into RL training and evaluates on τ-bench, τ²-bench, BFCL, and ACEBench. **People:** Weikang Zhao (**Meituan; Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences**), Xili Wang (**Meituan; Peking University**), Chengdi Ma (**Peking University**), and collaborators at **Meituan**.

text:

   **People:** Min Cai (University of Alberta); Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore); Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology); Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher); Xi Ye (University of Alberta and Amii).

query: methods improving user-centric agents with simulated users
text:
1. **[UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning](https://lifelongagent.github.io/Project-Lifelong-Agent/UserRL/index.html)** (2025). Trains agents through multi-turn interactions with simulated users, studying reward design, supervised warm starts, and simulator choice. **People:** Cheng Qian and Heng Ji — University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; Zuxin Liu and colleagues — Salesforce AI Research.

2. **[EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16523)** (2026). Uses a meta-agent to improve user simulators, environments, rewards, and training settings as agent learning progresses. **People:** Min Cai — University of Alberta; Dan Zhang — National University of Singapore; Gao Xing and Libin Ma — Kuaishou Technology; Zhaohui Xu — independent researcher; Xi Ye — University of Alberta and Amii.

3. **[Training Proactive and Personalized LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.02208v1)** (2025). Introduces **UserVille**, with preference-aware simulated users, and **PPP**, reinforcement learning that rewards task success, useful clarification, and personalization. **People:** Weiwei Sun, Xuhui Zhou, Weihua Du, Sean Welleck, Graham Neubig, Maarten Sap, and Yiming Yang — Carnegie Mellon University; Xingyao Wang — OpenHands.

4. **[CollabLLM: From Passive Responders to Active Collaborators](https://cs.stanford.edu/people/jure/pubs/collabllm-icml25.pdf)** (ICML 2025). Simulates future user conversations to reward responses that improve long-term collaboration; also validates improvements through a human study. **People:** Shirley Wu, Gavin Li, Weixin Cai, James Zou, and Jure Leskovec — Stanford University; Michel Galley, Baolin Peng, Hao Cheng, and Jianfeng Gao — Microsoft; Yao Dou — Georgia Tech.

5. **[Beyond Cooperative Simulators: Generating Realistic User Personas for Robust Evaluation of LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12894v1)** (2026). Evolves diverse user personas, including challenging communication behaviors, to improve simulator realism and agent robustness. **People:** Harshita Chopra, Kshitish Ghate, Aylin Caliskan, Chirag Shah, and Natasha Jaques — University of Washington; Tadayoshi Kohno — Georgetown University.
